Say "KEY" without the y: the little word that unlocks every clause. Eu acho que... = I think that...
I think it's going to rain today.
The same "ah" you say at the doctor's. Before feminine nouns it means the: a casa, a mesa.
Ela abriu a janela da sala.
She opened the living room window.
Written o, but unstressed it sounds like the "oo" in boot. Before masculine nouns: o carro, o livro.
O ônibus chegou atrasado de novo.
Say NOW while pinching your nose: that nasal ão is the sound of refusal. It goes before the verb: não sei.
Não gosto de café sem açúcar.
I don't like coffee without sugar.
jee (d before an ee sound becomes j)
Brazilians turn de into "jee", like the start of jeep. Copo de água = glass of water; sou de Recife = I'm from Recife.
Point at the thing in your listener's hand and hiss "S-S": esse livro, that book near you. Feminine: essa.
A tiny "ee" squeaking between two things, like a plus sign: arroz e feijão, rice and beans.
Quero arroz e feijão, por favor.
I'd like rice and beans, please.
oong (nasal, lips closed at the end)
Say "oom" and hum it through the nose, lips shut. One finger up: um café.
Me vê um pão de queijo?
Can I get a cheese bread?
A bus sign reading PARA CENTRO tells you where it goes: toward downtown. Spoken fast it shrinks to "pra".
"EH-oo", like the start of the English ew, but cheerful. You raise your hand: eu!
Add -a to um and you get the feminine version: uma casa, uma ideia. Counting: uma, duas, três.
Latin noster, the one in Pater Noster (Our Father). Feminine: nossa, which also works as Wow!
Nosso apartamento fica no terceiro andar.
Our apartment is on the third floor.
Latin cum, as in summa cum laude. Café com leite = coffee with milk, the classic Brazilian breakfast.
Vou ao cinema com minha irmã.
I'm going to the movies with my sister.
Spanish si, sounding just like English "see": if you see it, you believe it. Also the reflexive se.
Se chover, a gente fica em casa.
If it rains, we'll stay home.
de + o glued together = do. O carro do João = John's car (the car of the John).
A porta do quarto está fechada.
Latin per, as in per hour: por hora. Também: by, through, because of, thanks for.
o + s = os, the plural label: os meninos, os livros. Mixed groups also take os.
"EH-lee" sounds like Ellie, but it means HE. Feminine partner: ela.
"Mice"? I wanted cheese, BUT the mice ate it. Brazilians often say "mice" for mas.
I want to go, but I'm tired.
Latin in became em, nasalized. Em casa = at home, em cima = on top.
Latin bene, as in benefit and benevolent. Tudo bem? = all good? Bem cedo = very early.
"EE-soo!" Brazilians shout isso! meaning exactly, that's it! Points to the thing you just mentioned.
de + a = da. A casa da Maria = Maria's house. The feminine twin of do.
Spanish ¿cómo?, same spelling. Como vai? = How's it going? Also as: como sempre, as always.
sing (nasal, the g is barely heard)
Latin sic (thus, so), shortened and nasalized. Brazilians usually answer by repeating the verb instead: Quer? Quero!
a + s = as: as casas, as mulheres. Easy to tell apart from os by the vowel.
NOT English no! It's em + o: no carro = in the car. To say no, use não.
The keys are in the car.
Latin magis. Pronounced like "mice": more mice, more problems. Mais ou menos = more or less.
Quero mais um pedaço de bolo.
I want one more piece of cake.
Not "nah" as in no! It's em + a: na praia = on the beach, na rua = in the street.
A cat says "MEH-oo" and claims everything: MY sofa, MY bed. Meu Deus! = My God!
"Ah, KEY!" You found your keys right HERE. Spanish speakers: same as aquí.
You can leave the suitcase here.
Latin multum, as in multiply. It hides a nasal sound: say "MOOY-too" through the nose. Muito obrigado!
Thank you very much for the help.
Latin alter, as in alternative: the OTHER option. Outro café? = Another coffee?
Do you want another glass of juice?
Ella Fitzgerald: ELA is a SHE. Masculine partner: ele.
Latin istud. The T points closer than isso: isto is the thing in MY hand.
ow-GOONG (l at end of syllable sounds like w)
Al- + gum: like a piece of gum, SOME is in your pocket. Feminine: alguma.
Do you have any small change?
Latin facere, as in factory and fact: things are MADE there. Fazer café, fazer compras.
Vou fazer um bolo de chocolate.
I'm going to make a chocolate cake.
"Ah, KELLY!" you shout, pointing at that girl way over there. Farther away than esse.
That building over there is a hotel.
"ZHA!" like ta-da: it's ALREADY done. Já volto = I'll be right back.
Hamlet in Portuguese: Ser ou não ser. Use ser for who or what something is; estar for states.
I want to be a doctor one day.
Latin qualis, as in quality: WHICH kind? Qual é o seu nome? = What's your name?
Qual é a sua cor favorita?
a + a melt into one à, marked with a grave accent. Vou à praia = I'm going to the beach.
Tomorrow we're going to the beach early.
meu for him, minha for her: minha mãe, minha casa. nh sounds like the ny in canyon.
Minha mãe faz o melhor bolo.
My mom makes the best cake.
Sounds like "saw": I SAW ONLY one. Também: estou só = I'm alone. Só um minuto!
a + o = ao, said "ow". Vou ao médico = I'm going to the doctor.
I need to go to the bank today.
Al- (some) + -guém (from quem, who): some-who = someone. Tem alguém aí?
"TOO-DOO" list: EVERYTHING on it. Tudo bem? = Everything good? is the standard Brazilian hello.
chee (t before an ee sound becomes ch)
In Brazil te sounds like "chee" and goes before the verb: Te amo = I love you.
por (for) + que (what): for what reason? Because! Written together for because, apart (por que) for why.
Fiquei em casa porque estava chovendo.
I stayed home because it was raining.
have → haver, h silent. Its form há means there is / there are: há um problema.
Vai haver uma festa no sábado.
There's going to be a party on Saturday.
Just like "oy!" to get a friend's attention: the everyday Brazilian hello. Answer: Oi, tudo bem?
French entre, same spelling: entre nous, between us. Entre! also means Come in!
A farmácia fica entre o banco e a padaria.
The pharmacy is between the bank and the bakery.
Latin tu, Shakespeare's thou. Common in the South and Northeast of Brazil; elsewhere people say você.
Are you going to the party today?
Ante- as in anteroom: the room BEFORE the room. t before i-sound becomes ch: "AN-chees".
Lave as mãos antes do almoço.
Latin quando, used in Italian and Spanish too. Picture a clock with a question mark: quando?
When do you come back from your trip?
AGORA sounds like the Greek agora, the marketplace where everything happens right NOW. Agora não! = Not now!
From Italian ciao, respelled the Brazilian way. Rhymes with "wow": tchau, tchau!
Shortened from Vossa Mercê, Your Grace: a polite title that became everyday YOU. Takes the he/she verb: você é.
Sing "la la la" toward the far mountain: lá is THERE, far away. Lá em casa = at my place.
Stretch it out like "so..." while thinking: entããão... Brazilians start stories with it.
Então, o que vamos fazer hoje?
So, what are we doing today?
Latin tenere, as in tenant: someone who HAS a place. Eu tenho, você tem.
Same word in Spanish. Algo mais? = Anything else? asks every waiter.
Quer comer algo antes do filme?
Do you want to eat something before the movie?
Latin quem, the whom form. Quem é? = Who is it? at the door.
Latin unde (from where). The d before i-sound becomes j: "ON-jee". Onde fica? = Where is it?
English borrowed it: zip, zero, nada. De nada = it was nothing, you're welcome.
French ou, same spelling. Café ou chá? = Coffee or tea?
Do you prefer the beach or the mountains?
Latin causa (a matter, a case) wore down into coisa. Uma coisa = a thing; coisa nenhuma = nothing at all.
Tenho uma coisa para te contar.
I have something to tell you.
Latin dicere, as in dictate and diction. Quer dizer = it means (it wants to say).
O que você quer dizer com isso?
What do you mean by that?
Latin nec unum, not even one. Nenhum problema = no problem at all.
Não tenho nenhum plano para hoje.
I don't have any plans for today.
Spanish desde, same word. Desde 2010 = since 2010. Desde criança = since childhood.
procure → procurar: to obtain by searching. Estou procurando = I'm looking for.
Vou procurar um apartamento perto do trabalho.
I'm going to look for an apartment near work.
você + s = vocês: the Brazilian y'all. It takes the they form of the verb: vocês são.
Do you guys want pizza or a burger?
Matches você: o seu carro = your car. Also his or her, so Brazilians often prefer dele / dela for clarity.
during → durante, both from endure: for the whole time. Durante o filme = during the movie.
I slept during the whole trip.
Spanish mismo. O mesmo = the same; mesmo assim = even so; sério mesmo? = really?
We have the same last name.
Not está (is)! No accent, stress on ES: esta casa = this house. The accented está is a verb.
ele + s = eles: a whole group of HE's. Feminine group: elas.
Latin nos, as in the Spanish nosotros. Everyday speech often swaps it for a gente.
We're going out for dinner tonight.
The feminine form of seu: a sua casa, a sua bolsa. It matches the thing owned, not the owner.
Your bag is on the chair.
de + os = dos. O time dos meninos = the boys' team.
A casa dos meus avós é antiga.
Latin totus, as in total. Todo dia = every day; o dia todo = the whole day.
Ela corre todo dia de manhã.
Two jobs: object pronoun (ele nos ajudou = he helped us) and em + os (nos fins de semana = on weekends).
Ele nos convidou para o casamento.
He invited us to the wedding.
After para, de, sem: para mim = for me. Hum it like "me" through the nose.
Latin mecum turned inside out: com + migo. Vem comigo! = Come with me!
Você quer ir comigo ao mercado?
Do you want to go to the market with me?
French bon, as in bon voyage. Bom dia = good morning. Feminine: boa.
Latin videre, as in video and vision. Vamos ver = let's see.
Quero ver esse filme no cinema.
I want to see that movie at the theater.
Latin iste. Like esta, but for masculine nouns: este livro. In speech Brazilians often use esse instead.
Este ano vou aprender a nadar.
This year I'm going to learn to swim.
Casa Blanca is the White House. Em casa = at home; a single s between vowels sounds like z.
Minha casa tem um quintal grande.
My house has a big backyard.
de + ela = dela: of her. Clearer than sua, so Brazilians say a bolsa dela = her bag.
A bolsa dela ficou no táxi.
Her bag was left in the taxi.
des- + culpa (guilt, as in culprit): removing the guilt. Desculpa! = Sorry!
"Ah, kilo!" Pointing at that big sack over there: what is THAT? Used for things, never people.
O que é aquilo no céu?
What is that in the sky?
Latin numquam: not once, ever. Nunca mais = never again.
certain → certeza. Tem certeza? = Are you sure? Com certeza! = Absolutely!
"At 8" sounds like até: wait UNTIL 8. Até logo! = See you soon!
A loja fica aberta até as dez.
The store stays open until ten.
"A-SING": sing it LIKE THIS. Assim mesmo = just like that.
Do it like this, it's easier.
de + ele = dele: of him. Brazilians love it because it is clearer than seu: o carro dele = his car.
O carro dele quebrou de novo.
The famous untranslatable word: the ache of missing someone. Estou com saudade = I miss you.
Estou com saudade da minha avó.
Parler in French, hablar in Spanish, falar here: fables are things spoken. Fala português?
Spanish señora, with nh instead of ñ. A senhora = polite you for an older woman.
"Ah, INDA-ed, it's STILL raining." Ainda não = not yet.
Musicians know tempo: the TIME of a song. Also weather: o tempo está bom.
Não tenho tempo para almoçar hoje.
I don't have time for lunch today.
Two nasal hums, "tam-BENG", like a drum and a bell joining in TOO. Eu também! = Me too!
Latin ire, as in exit (ex + ire, go out). Vou, vai, vamos: the forms look nothing alike.
Tomorrow I need to go to the dentist.
Dad loves PIE: pai rhymes with it. Os pais = the parents.
Latin super, as in superior: over, ABOUT. Um livro sobre o Brasil = a book about Brazil.
Latin vicis, as in vice-president: the one whose TURN comes next. Uma vez = once; sua vez = your turn.
É a minha vez de pagar.
"NANG", a door slamming: NOT EVEN a chance. Nem eu = me neither.
He didn't even look at me.
The opposite of alguém (someone): ninguém, no-who. Ninguém sabe = nobody knows.
en + quanto (how much): for as long as. Enquanto você dorme = while you sleep.
Ela lê enquanto espera o ônibus.
She reads while she waits for the bus.
favor → favor, identical. Por favor = please (by favor). Me faz um favor?
Can you do me a favor?
"Day-POISE": first the day, then the poise. Depois a gente vê = we'll see later.
Depois do jantar, vamos ver um filme.
After dinner, we'll watch a movie.
Rhymes with não, but it pumps things up: tão bonito = so pretty. Tão... quanto = as... as.
Latin melior, as in ameliorate (make better). O melhor = the best.
Esse é o melhor pastel da feira.
This is the best pastel at the street market.
Say "MY" while humming through the nose: MY mom. Dia das Mães = Mother's Day.
My mom lives in the countryside.
tal (such) + vez (time): at such a time, MAYBE. Talvez amanhã = maybe tomorrow.
Talvez eu chegue um pouco atrasado.
Maybe I'll arrive a bit late.
Spanish hola, with the stress at the end. A bit more formal than oi.
obliged → obrigado: I'm much obliged. A woman says obrigada.
Latin nox, as in nocturnal and equinox. Boa noite = good evening or good night.
The tu version of mim: para ti = for you. Sounds like "chee" because t before i becomes ch.
Latin semper, as in the US Marines' Semper Fi (always faithful). Como sempre = as always.
Latin dies, as in diary. Masculine despite the -a: o dia, bom dia!
certain → certo. Tá certo! = All right! Errado is its opposite.
Do you have the right address?
Latin vita, as in vitamin and vital. Minha vida = my life, also a sweet nickname.
A vida no campo é tranquila.
Life in the countryside is peaceful.
Latin sine, as in sine qua non. Café sem açúcar = coffee without sugar.
I left home without an umbrella.
state → estar: the STATE you are in right now. Estou cansado; ser is for what you are.
Vou estar no escritório até as seis.
I'll be at the office until six.
Latin homo, as in Homo sapiens. The h is silent.
Aquele homem é o dono da padaria.
That man is the bakery owner.
Latin voluntas, as in voluntary. Estou com vontade de = I feel like.
Estou com vontade de comer pizza.
by the / through the / for the
por + o = pelo: passear pelo parque = stroll through the park. Obrigado pelo café!
We went through the city center.
to stay / to become / to be located
A FIg tree that never moves: it STAYS put. Fica perto = it's nearby; fiquei feliz = I became happy.
I'm going to stay home today.
Latin tantus. Tanto faz = it doesn't matter (either is so much the same).
Nunca vi tanto carro na rua.
I've never seen so many cars on the street.
clear → claro, as in clarity. Claro! = Of course! Azul claro = light blue.
-dade = -ty: verity → verdade. É verdade? = Is it true?
type → tipo. Teens fill sentences with tipo, exactly like English "like".
Que tipo de música você gosta?
What kind of music do you like?
Spanish señor. O senhor = polite you for an older man.
Would you like more coffee, sir?
Spanish apenas means barely; here it means ONLY. A bit more formal than só.
Only two students were absent today.
French travail, as in travel (once hard work). Vou para o trabalho = I'm going to work.
Latin sapere, as in Homo sapiens, the one who KNOWS. Sei nadar = I know how to swim.
Do you want to know a secret?
Latin denarius, the Roman coin that also gave dinar. Dinheiro vivo = cash.
I forgot the money at home.
"Ah-EE!" yelled at someone over THERE, near you. E aí? = What's up?
Latin paucus, as in paucity (scarcity). Um pouco = a little.
Fala um pouco mais devagar, por favor.
Speak a little more slowly, please.
grand → grande. Grande São Paulo = Greater São Paulo.
They live in a big house.
Latin hodie, hoc die, on this day. Hoje é sexta! = Today is Friday!
Latin mulier. Minha mulher = my wife, informally.
A mulher do vizinho é professora.
The neighbor's wife is a teacher.
Latin foris, as in foreign: from outside. Jantar fora = to eat out.
As crianças estão brincando lá fora.
Latin filius, as in filial. Os filhos = the children. Feminine: filha.
My son is five years old.
Latin eccum hac. Mainly in set phrases in Brazil: vem cá! = come here! Para cá = over here.
Vem cá, quero te mostrar uma coisa.
Come here, I want to show you something.
serious → sério. Sério? = Really? is the classic reaction.
Sério que você nunca viu o mar?
Seriously, you've never seen the sea?
Latin nomen, as in nominate. Qual é o seu nome? = What's your name?
Qual é o nome do seu cachorro?
Latin dare, as in donate and data (things given). Dá pra = it's possible.
Vou dar um livro para ela.
I'm going to give her a book.
tempt / attempt → tentar. Tenta de novo! = Try again!
"Sigh-EAR": you SIGH as you LEAVE the party. Saída = exit.
Ele acabou de sair de casa.
quantity → quanto. Quanto custa? = How much is it?
pensive → pensar. Penso em você = I think about you.
I need to think before deciding.
French mal, as in malfunction. Dormi mal = I slept badly. The l sounds like w.
A VOLT shoots around the circuit and comes back: a full turn. Dar uma volta = take a stroll.
Vamos dar uma volta no parque?
Shall we take a walk in the park?
Latin mundus, as in mundane (worldly). O mundo todo = the whole world.
She wants to travel the world.
minus → menos. Mais ou menos = more or less, so-so.
Hoje está menos frio que ontem.
It's less cold today than yesterday.
Every English speaker knows amigo from Spanish. Feminine: amiga.
Meu amigo vai passar aqui mais tarde.
My friend is going to stop by later.
em + boa hora (at a good hour) shortened. Ir embora = to leave; embora = although.
problem → problema, masculine despite the -a. Sem problema = no problem.
Tem um problema com o meu computador.
There's a problem with my computer.
car → carro. The double rr is a breathy h: "KAH-hoo".
My car is at the mechanic's.
Latin latus, as in lateral. Do lado = next door. Ao lado de = beside.
Latin novus, as in novel and nova. Ano Novo = New Year.
I bought a new cell phone.
part → parte. A maior parte = most of it.
Essa é a melhor parte do filme.
This is the best part of the movie.
primary → primeiro. Primeiro andar = first floor.
Hoje é o primeiro dia de aula.
Today is the first day of class.
Latin locus, as in location. Em primeiro lugar = in the first place.
From volta, the turn: you turn around and come BACK. Já volto = I'll be right back.
A que horas você vai voltar?
What time are you coming back?
Latin de intro, as in intro and interior. Dentro de casa = inside the house.
A chave está dentro da gaveta.
The key is inside the drawer.
family → família. The stress falls on MEE.
Passo o Natal com a minha família.
I spend Christmas with my family.
Muhammad Ali stands right THERE, a few steps away: closer than lá.
O banheiro fica ali à direita.
The bathroom is right there on the right.
hah-ZOWNG (r at the start sounds like h)
reason → razão (-son → -são). Você tem razão = you're right.
idea → ideia, just add an i. Boa ideia! = Good idea!
hour → hora, silent h in both. Que horas são? = What time is it?
Já está na hora de dormir.
police → polícia. The stress is on LEE. Policial = police officer.
form → forma. Em forma = in shape; de forma nenhuma = no way.
Ela vai à academia para ficar em forma.
She goes to the gym to stay in shape.
case → caso. Em caso de chuva = in case of rain. Também: um caso = an affair.
Em caso de dúvida, me liga.
In case of doubt, call me.
Latin amor, as in amorous and Cupid's other name. Meu amor = my love.
Ela é o amor da minha vida.
She is the love of my life.
person → pessoa. Always feminine, even for a man: ele é uma pessoa legal.
Ele é uma pessoa muito calma.
He is a very calm person.
Latin caput, as in capital and decapitate. Dor de cabeça = headache.
press → pressa: time is PRESSING. Estou com pressa = I'm in a hurry.
Sorry, I'm in a hurry right now.
Latin adiutare, as in adjutant (an officer's helper). Posso ajudar? = Can I help?
Você pode me ajudar com a mala?
Can you help me with the suitcase?
Latin tardus, as in tardy: LATE. As a noun: a tarde, the afternoon. Boa tarde!
Let's go to the park in the afternoon.
moment → momento. Um momento, por favor = One moment, please.
Um momento, já vou te atender.
One moment, I'll be right with you.
prompt → pronto: ready on the spot. Pronto! also means There, done!
-dade = -ty: city → cidade. Cidade Maravilhosa = Rio's nickname.
São Paulo é uma cidade enorme.
São Paulo is a huge city.
encounter → encontrar. Vamos nos encontrar? = Shall we meet up?
front → frente. Em frente = straight ahead; na frente de = in front of.
Te espero na frente do cinema.
I'll wait for you in front of the movie theater.
to pass / to spend (time) / to iron
pass → passar. Passar as férias = to spend the holidays. Also passar roupa = to iron clothes.
Vamos passar o fim de semana na praia.
We're going to spend the weekend at the beach.
"Day SHAH!" says the boss: LET the workers go home, LEAVE it for tomorrow. Me deixa! = Leave me alone!
You can leave your bag here.
Latin gens, as in gentle and genealogy. A gente = we in everyday speech: a gente vai.
enter → entrar. Pode entrar! = Come on in!
Pode entrar, a porta está aberta.
Come in, the door is open.
"She GOT here!" Chegar = to arrive. Chega! = That's enough!
O voo vai chegar às dez.
The flight will arrive at ten.
The verb from trabalho: trabalhar. Trabalho em casa = I work from home.
I don't need to work today.
quasi- → quase: quasi-official, almost official. Quase nunca = hardly ever.
Spanish mañana: the land of tomorrow. Até amanhã! = See you tomorrow!
history / story → história, silent h. Conta uma história! = Tell a story!
Spanish hermano lost the h and nasalized: irmão. Irmã = sister.
Meu irmão mais novo estuda direito.
mortal / mortuary → morrer. Morrer de rir = to die laughing.
Quase morri de rir com essa piada.
I almost died laughing at that joke.
manner → maneira. De maneira nenhuma = no way.
Essa é a maneira certa de fazer.
This is the right way to do it.
The noun from ajudar. Preciso de ajuda! = I need help!
Obrigado pela ajuda com a mudança.
Thanks for the help with the move.
portal / porch → porta. Porta-malas = car trunk (door for suitcases).
"MAY-do" sounds like "May doom": FEAR of what's coming. Ter medo de = to be afraid of.
Spanish camino, as in the Camino de Santiago pilgrimage route. No caminho = on the way.
Passo na padaria no caminho de casa.
I stop at the bakery on the way home.
Latin venire, as in venue and convene. Venha! = Come! Vem cá = come here.
Você pode vir à minha festa?
Can you come to my party?
Felix the Cat always grins: a FELIX is a HAPPY one. Feliz aniversário! = Happy birthday!
French ouïr, as in the courtroom cry "Oyez!" (hear ye). Ouvir música = to listen to music.
Gosto de ouvir música no carro.
I like listening to music in the car.
The matador KILLS the bull. Matar a saudade = to cure your longing by visiting someone.
This heat is going to kill me!
Same in Spanish. Cada um = each one; cada vez mais = more and more.
"A con-test, eh?" Something exciting is going to HAPPEN. O que aconteceu? = What happened?
Latin annus, as in annual and anniversary. Feliz Ano Novo! = Happy New Year!
Ela faz dez anos este ano.
hah-PAHSS (r at the start sounds like h)
"Ha, PASS!" says the young GUY waving off homework. Rapaz! is also a cry of surprise, like Man!
That young man works at the pharmacy.
cause → causa. Por causa de = because of.
Chegamos tarde por causa do trânsito.
We arrived late because of the traffic.
filho (son) + a = filha (daughter). nh and lh sound like the ny and ll in canyon and million.
A filha dela já está na faculdade.
Her daughter is already in college.
lever / elevate → levar: lift it and TAKE it with you. Levar o cachorro = take the dog.
Não esquece de levar o guarda-chuva.
Don't forget to take the umbrella.
count / account → conta. A conta, por favor = The check, please.
Not your arm (that's braço)! It's armament: a weapon. Arma de fogo = firearm.
The police officer put away the gun.
pessoa (person) + -al = personal. Brazilians greet a group with Oi, pessoal! = Hi, everyone!
A QUARTER of the house is your BEDROOM. Also means fourth and a quarter.
Meu quarto fica no segundo andar.
My bedroom is on the second floor.
a Deus = to God, like French adieu: a heavy goodbye. For everyday leaving, use tchau.
Ela disse adeus e entrou no trem.
She said goodbye and boarded the train.
guy / dude (as a noun: face, f)
Not "dear" (that's querido)! O cara = the guy, Brazil's version of dude. A cara = the face.
joint / junction → juntos: joined together. Feminine: juntas.
Spanish mañana means both tomorrow and morning; Portuguese splits them: amanhã / manhã. Bom dia covers the greeting.
Corro todos os dias de manhã.
important → importante, add -e. O mais importante = the most important thing.
I have an important meeting tomorrow.
can / to be able to / power
potent / power → poder. Posso? = May I? Also a noun: o poder = the power.
Will you be able to come tomorrow?
Latin aqua, as in aquarium. Água de coco = coconut water.
Me dá um copo de água?
Can you give me a glass of water?
French commencer, as in commencement. O filme vai começar!
A aula vai começar em cinco minutos.
Class is going to start in five minutes.
"PEHR-to" like "pert": a pert little shop right NEAR here. Perto de = close to.
Is there a supermarket near here?
Spanish semana, from Latin septimana (seven days). Fim de semana = weekend.
Vejo você na semana que vem.
use → usar. Also wear: usar óculos = wear glasses.
corpse / corporal → corpo. Living bodies too: corpo humano.
chef / chief → chefe. Not only in kitchens: meu chefe = my boss.
Meu chefe me deu o dia de folga.
My boss gave me the day off.
jog / joke → jogo: playful fun. Jogo de futebol = soccer match.
Você vai ver o jogo hoje?
Are you going to watch the game today?
The noun of falar: what you say. Fala sério! = Get real! Uma fala = a line in a play.
Ele esqueceu a fala dele na peça.
He forgot his line in the play.
"MOSS-a" sounds like moss on a lovely old garden where a YOUNG WOMAN reads. Moça! = Miss! to call a waitress.
Miss, could you bring the menu?
-mente = -ly: real → really. The r at the start sounds like h.
Latin terra, as in terrain and territory. A Terra = planet Earth.
As crianças estão brincando na terra.
The kids are playing in the dirt.
"ON-tame": ONce tame, back YESTERDAY. Ontem à noite = last night.
Spanish comer, same. Vamos comer? = Let's eat? Comida = food.
O que você quer comer hoje?
What do you want to eat today?
dormitory / dormant → dormir. Durma bem! = Sleep well!
I need to sleep early tonight.
school / scholar → escola, with an e in front as Portuguese loves. Escola de samba!
Meu filho vai a pé para a escola.
Not a brand logo! Até logo = see you soon. Penso, logo existo = I think, therefore I am.
I'll be back soon, wait for me.
From querer, to want or love: wanted = beloved. Querido amigo = dear friend.
Honey, have you seen my keys?
French fin, at the end of old films. Fim de semana = weekend (end of week).
Gostei muito do fim do livro.
I really liked the end of the book.
agent → agente. Careful: written together it's an agent; a gente (two words) means we.
O agente de viagens reservou o hotel.
The travel agent booked the hotel.
French équipe, as in equipped: a team kitted out together. Brazil says equipe; Portugal says equipa.
colleague → colega. Works for coworkers and classmates; a colega for a woman.
Meu colega de trabalho faz aniversário hoje.
My coworker has a birthday today.
married → marido: the MARRIED man. Feminine pair: esposa or mulher.
Meu marido cozinha melhor que eu.
My husband cooks better than I do.
core / courage → coração: the core of you. -ção is said "sowng".
Ela tem um coração de ouro.
She has a heart of gold.
vivid / survive → viver. Viver bem = to live well. For where you live, prefer morar.
I want to live for many years.
"Pa-RAH!" a traffic cop's whistle: STOP! Pare is on every Brazilian stop sign.
The bus is going to stop here.
second → segundo. Both an order (segundo lugar) and a slice of a minute.
Ele ficou em segundo lugar na corrida.
He came in second in the race.
Latin manus, as in manual and manicure. Feminine despite -o: a mão.
Italian basso, a LOW singing voice. Fala baixo = speak quietly. Embaixo = below.
Meu irmão é mais baixo que eu.
My brother is shorter than me.
major → maior. Maior de idade = of legal age.
Esse é o maior shopping da cidade.
This is the biggest mall in the city.
A line down the MIDDLE splits it in half. Meio-dia = noon. Meio cansado = kind of tired.
Latin malus, as in malware. Sounds the same as mal (badly); mau is the adjective: um mau dia.
Ele não é um mau menino.
Andante in music = a WALKING pace. As a noun: o terceiro andar = the third floor.
Gosto de andar na praia de manhã.
I like walking on the beach in the morning.
rapid → rápido. Stress on the first syllable.
number / numeral → número. Qual é o seu número? = What's your number?
Me passa o seu número de telefone.
festival / fiesta → festa. Festa Junina = the June harvest party.
Vai ter festa na casa do Pedro.
There's going to be a party at Pedro's house.
to fetch / to pick up / to seek
Spanish buscar. Vou te buscar = I'll pick you up.
Vou buscar as crianças na escola.
I'm going to pick up the kids from school.
perdition → perder. Perder o ônibus = miss the bus.
I don't want to miss the flight.
to wait / to hope / to expect
Spanish esperar, from Latin sperare, as in desperate (without hope). Espera aí! = Hang on!
irmão minus the o: irmã. The tilde makes the final a nasal.
possible → possível: -ble becomes -vel. Se possível = if possible.
Is it possible to change the date?
contra-, as in contradict and contraband. Contra a parede = against the wall.
"A KABOOM!" and it's all OVER. Acabei de chegar = I just arrived.
count / recount → contar: to count numbers or recount a story. Conta! = Tell me!
I'm going to tell you some news.
"Oh, LYAH!" you gasp as you LOOK. Olha! = Look!
Olha só que lindo esse lugar!
Just look how beautiful this place is!
Not a pen (that's caneta)! Que pena! = What a shame! Vale a pena = it's worth it. Old quills were feathers.
Vale a pena visitar o museu.
long → longe: a long way off. Longe daqui = far from here.
O aeroporto fica longe do centro.
The airport is far from downtown.
Latin petere, as in petition. Pedir uma pizza = to order a pizza.
Shall we order a pizza tonight?
strange / stranger → estranho. nh = ny, like canyon.
Ouvi um barulho estranho lá fora.
I heard a strange noise outside.
facile / facility → fácil. Final l sounds like w.
Kids at the BRINK of a pool, splashing and playing. Tô brincando = I'm just kidding.
As crianças adoram brincar no parque.
The kids love playing in the park.
French bébé, same sound. Brazil writes bebê; Portugal bebé.
O bebê está dormindo no quarto.
The baby is sleeping in the bedroom.
plan → plano. Plano de saúde = health insurance plan.
Qual é o plano para sábado?
A VELvet armchair, worn and OLD. Meu velho = my old man (dad).
to manage / to be able / to get
consequence / get → conseguir: you GET there in the end. Consegui! = I did it!
passed → passado: what has passed. Semana passada = last week.
I don't want to talk about the past.
A TOMATO juice: you TAKE a sip and DRINK. Tomar banho = take a shower.
I'm going to take a quick shower.
"Jaunty" mood after a good DINNER. Both noun and verb: vamos jantar?
de + pressa (hurry): in a hurry. Anda depressa! = Walk faster!
Vem depressa, o filme já começou!
Come quickly, the movie already started!
"Pear GOON" asking a QUESTION with a puzzled face. Fazer uma pergunta = ask a question.
to take off / to take out
"Tear-AH": you TEAR it off. Tirar uma foto = take a picture.
Can you take a picture of us?
Spanish pequeño. Feminine pequena. Pequeno-almoço is breakfast only in Portugal.
I live in a small apartment.
discover → descobrir: un-cover. Descobri que = I found out that.
Descobri um café ótimo perto daqui.
I discovered a great café near here.
Italian sala, as in salon. Sala de aula = classroom; sala de estar = living room.
Let's watch TV in the living room.
telephone → telefone, ph becomes f. Usually the landline; cell phone is celular.
The phone rang in the middle of the night.
err / error → errado. Número errado = wrong number.
Acho que você pegou o ônibus errado.
I think you took the wrong bus.
vivid / vivacious → vivo. Ao vivo = live (broadcast).
O show vai passar ao vivo.
The concert will be broadcast live.
"Many NEE-na" dolls: a GIRL's collection. Masculine: menino.
A menina está aprendendo a ler.
The girl is learning to read.
current / courier → correr: things that run. Correr risco = run a risk.
Eu gosto de correr no parque.
I like running in the park.
mutate → mudar. Mudar de casa = move house.
Vamos mudar de apartamento em março.
sense / sentiment → sentir. Sinto muito = I'm very sorry.
"Karma" without the r: good KARMA, good BED. Ir para a cama = go to bed.
Spanish comida, from comer (eat). Comida caseira = home cooking.
Italian basta! = enough! Bastante = plenty, quite a lot.
parable → palavra: both come from Greek parabole. Dou minha palavra = I give my word.
different → diferente, one f and an extra e.
Cada cidade tem um sotaque diferente.
Each city has a different accent.
Latin vox, as in vocal and vox pop. Em voz alta = out loud.
de + mais (more): more than enough. Slang: Esse show foi demais! = That show was awesome!
I ate too much at lunch.
pay → pagar: same p-a start. Pagar a conta = pay the bill.
Preciso marcar uma consulta com o médico.
I need to make an appointment with the doctor.
sequel / sequence → seguir: what follows. Siga em frente = keep going straight.
Você pode seguir essa rua até o final.
You can follow this street to the end.
French sang, as in sanguine. Doar sangue = to donate blood.
Ele não gosta de ver sangue.
unique → único. Filho único = only child.
credit / credible → acreditar: to give credit. Não acredito! = I can't believe it!
local → local, as a noun too: o local da festa = the party venue.
Qual é o local da reunião?
Where is the meeting being held?
proper / property → próprio. Meu próprio carro = my own car.
Ela quer abrir o próprio negócio.
She wants to open her own business.
French pays, as in peasant (a country person). Two syllables: pa-ÍS.
O Brasil é um país enorme.
fort / fortitude → forte. Café forte = strong coffee.
to leave / to depart / to break
depart → partir. A partir de hoje = starting today.
O trem vai partir às seis.
The train will depart at six.
special → especial, with an extra e at the front.
French livre and Spanish libro, from Latin liber, as in library. Livraria = bookstore (false friend!).
rest → resto: what's left. O resto do dia = the rest of the day.
I saved the rest of the pizza.
Latin aer, as in aerial. Ar-condicionado = air conditioning.
Abre a janela para entrar ar.
Open the window to let some air in.
hospital → hospital, silent h, final l sounds like w.
Ela trabalha no hospital à noite.
She works at the hospital at night.
Not a website (that's site)! In Brazil, um sítio is a small country farm where families spend weekends.
Passamos o feriado no sítio do meu tio.
We spent the holiday at my uncle's farm.
to call / to turn on / to connect
ligament → ligar: it ties things together. Te ligo = I'll call you; ligar a TV = turn on the TV.
Call me when you get there.
minute → minuto. Só um minuto! = Just a minute!
Wait a minute, I'll be right back.
sense → sentido. Faz sentido = makes sense; sentido único = one-way.
That makes no sense at all.
direct / right → direito. Faculdade de direito = law school. Lado direito = right side.
coffee / café → café. Café da manhã = breakfast (morning coffee).
Do you want to have a coffee with me?
create / creature → criança: a little creation. Always feminine: a criança.
A criança está brincando no quintal.
The child is playing in the backyard.
Latin lux, as in lucid and lux. Conta de luz = electricity bill.
film → filme, add -e. Filme de terror = horror movie.
Vamos ver um filme hoje à noite?
Shall we watch a movie tonight?
music → música. Stress on MOO. Also means a single song.
Essa música me lembra a praia.
This song reminds me of the beach.
posit / deposit → pôr. The hat (^) separates it from the preposition por. Pôr do sol = sunset.
Pode pôr o prato na mesa.
You can put the plate on the table.
Latin quaerere (to seek), as in query: what are you seeking? Quero = I want.
O que você vai querer de sobremesa?
What would you like for dessert?
Latin focus, the fireplace at the center of a home. Fogos = fireworks.
Cuidado com o fogo da churrasqueira.
Would you like something to drink?
to win / to earn / to get
gain → ganhar. Ganhar presente = get a gift.
Quem vai ganhar o jogo hoje?
Who's going to win the game today?
point → ponto. Ponto de ônibus = bus stop.
Te espero no ponto de ônibus.
I'll wait for you at the bus stop.
maintain → manter, from mão (hand) + ter (hold): hold in hand.
precise → precisar: what you need precisely. Preciso de = I need.
HOO-ah (r at the start sounds like h)
French rue, as in Paris street signs. Na rua = in the street, outside.
I live on the street with the bakery.
pedal / pedestrian → pé. A pé = on foot.
Vou a pé para o trabalho.
ultimate → último. A última vez = the last time.
Esse é o último ônibus da noite.
This is the last bus of the night.
peel → pele: the skin you peel off fruit. Pelé the footballer is a different word!
"SAY-do": SAY "do it EARLY". Acordar cedo = wake up early.
Tomorrow I need to wake up early.
Italian bocca, as in a big open mouth at the Bocca della Verità. Boca de urna = exit poll.
Don't talk with your mouth full!
juvenile → jovem. Os jovens = young people.
Ele é jovem demais para dirigir.
comprador / compare prices → comprar. Fazer compras = go shopping.
I'm going to buy bread at the bakery.
spouse → esposa. Masculine: esposo, though marido is more common.
The verb of jogo: jogar futebol = play soccer. Jogar fora = throw away.
Shall we play soccer on Saturday?
amigo with -a: a female friend. Minha melhor amiga = my best friend.
secure → seguro. As a noun, seguro do carro = car insurance.
Esse bairro é seguro à noite?
Is this neighborhood safe at night?
-tion → -tão: question → questão. Faço questão = I insist.
encounter → encontro. Primeiro encontro = first date.
Hoje tenho um encontro com ela.
Today I have a date with her.
Latin canis, as in canine. In Brazil, cachorro is the everyday word; cão sounds literary.
negotiate → negócio. Fechar negócio = close a deal.
Ele abriu um negócio de comida.
Italian allegro, a lively tempo in music. Porto Alegre = Happy Port.
Ela é uma pessoa muito alegre.
She is a very cheerful person.
I just sent you a message.
proximity → próximo. Próxima semana = next week.
I'm getting off at the next stop.
Italian bagno. Tomar banho = to shower; banheiro = bathroom.
Vou tomar banho antes do jantar.
I'm going to shower before dinner.
From chamar (to call): a call. Fazer a chamada = take attendance.
Perdi uma chamada da minha mãe.
I missed a call from my mom.
nova (new) + -mente: anew. Same as de novo, a little more formal.
Por favor, tente novamente mais tarde.
future → futuro. No futuro = in the future.
The verb of pergunta. To ask FOR something is pedir; to ask a question is perguntar.
notice → notícia. As notícias = the news. Boa notícia! = Good news!
Tenho uma notícia boa para você.
I have some good news for you.
French clamer / English claim: call out loud. Como você se chama? = What's your name?
Latin capillus, as in capillary (hair-thin). Cortar o cabelo = get a haircut.
group → grupo. Grupo do WhatsApp = the inevitable family chat.
Ela estuda em grupo com os colegas.
She studies in a group with her classmates.
doctor → doutor. Brazilians also use it as a respectful title for lawyers and bosses.
O doutor já vai te atender.
The doctor will see you shortly.
liberty → livre. Free of charge is grátis. Tempo livre = free time.
voyage → viagem. Boa viagem! = Have a good trip!
conversation → conversa, just chop the end. Conversa fiada = small talk, nonsense.
We had a long conversation yesterday.
to flee / to run away / to escape
fugitive → fugir. O cachorro fugiu = the dog ran away.
O gato tentou fugir pela janela.
The cat tried to escape through the window.
list → lista. Lista de compras = shopping list.
From escrever (to write): the place where you write. Also a law firm: escritório de advocacia.
final → final. No final = in the end. Final de semana = weekend.
I liked the ending of the movie.
Italian alto, the HIGH voice in a choir. Fala mais alto = speak louder.
Spanish bonito, same word. Feminine: bonita. Que dia bonito!
"SHOWN" on the FLOOR: everything you drop is shown down there. Rhymes with não.
The book fell on the floor.
camp / campus → campo. Campo de futebol = soccer field.
Eles moram no campo, longe da cidade.
They live in the countryside, far from the city.
O dia estava perfeito para praia.
The day was perfect for the beach.
Spanish tío. Kids call any grown-up man tio. Tia = aunt.
I completely forgot about the meeting.
brief / brevity → breve. Em breve = soon.
O filme chega em breve aos cinemas.
The movie is coming to theaters soon.
remedy → remédio. Tomar remédio = take medicine. Farmácia sells them.
Não esquece de tomar o remédio.
Don't forget to take your medicine.
normal → normal, but the final l sounds like w.
É normal sentir um pouco de medo.
It's normal to feel a bit afraid.
A MESA in the desert is a flat-topped mountain: a giant TABLE. Pôr a mesa = set the table.
simple → simples, with a final s even in the singular.
I'm working on a new project.
employ → emprego. Procurar emprego = look for a job.
line → linha. Linha do metrô = subway line; linha de costura = thread.
Qual linha de metrô vai para o centro?
real → real, and royal too. O real is Brazil's money: dez reais.
"A soon-to" be TOPIC of gossip. Mudar de assunto = change the subject.
order → ordem. Em ordem = in order; tudo em ordem = everything's fine.
fund / fundamental → fundo: the base. No fundo = at the back, deep down.
I sat at the back of the bus.
accident → acidente, one c less and an -e.
There was an accident on the highway.
mode → modo. De modo geral = generally.
Gosto do seu modo de falar.
I like your way of speaking.
Ainda estou esperando a resposta dele.
I'm still waiting for his answer.
mama → mamãe, ending in a nasal hum. Papai = daddy.
aviation → avião. De avião = by plane.
error → erro. Cometer um erro = make a mistake.
Achei um erro no seu texto.
I found a mistake in your text.
verdade (truth) + -eiro: full of truth. Um amigo verdadeiro = a true friend.
-dade = -ty, but here age hides inside: idade. Qual é a sua idade? = How old are you?
Com que idade você aprendeu a nadar?
At what age did you learn to swim?
fantastic → fantástico. Also the name of Brazil's famous Sunday-night TV show.
space → espaço, with Portugal's favorite extra e in front.
Não tem espaço no carro para a mala.
There's no room in the car for the suitcase.
service → serviço. Área de serviço = laundry area of an apartment.
O serviço desse restaurante é ótimo.
The service at this restaurant is great.
Latin legere, as in legible and lecture. Leio, lê, lemos: short and sweet.
Gosto de ler antes de dormir.
I like to read before bed.
Spanish loco, everyone's word for crazy. Louco por = crazy about.
Esse trânsito vai me deixar louco.
This traffic is going to drive me crazy.
to know (a person or place) / to meet
cognition / recognize → conhecer. Prazer em te conhecer = nice to meet you.
Quero conhecer a Bahia um dia.
I want to visit Bahia one day.
Spanish lindo. Brazilians say it constantly: Que lindo! = How lovely!
Que lindo esse pôr do sol!
Preciso de uma informação, por favor.
Latin aperire, as in aperture (an opening). Abre a porta! = Open the door!
A loja vai abrir às nove.
The store will open at nine.
perceive → perceber. Não percebi = I didn't notice.
Não percebi que você estava aqui.
I didn't notice you were here.
program → programa, masculine despite -a. Also a night out: Qual é o programa hoje?
Qual é o programa para hoje à noite?
Latin sol, as in solar. The final l sounds like w: "sow". Pegar sol = sunbathe.
Hoje o sol está muito forte.
The sun is very strong today.
Ele simplesmente foi embora sem falar nada.
He simply left without saying anything.
case / cash box → caixa. Caixa eletrônico = ATM; o caixa = the cashier.
hotel → hotel, silent h and final l like w.
O hotel fica perto da praia.
The hotel is near the beach.
gusto / disgust → gostar. Always with de: gosto de você = I like you.
You're going to like this place.
Latin ecclesia, as in ecclesiastical, worn down to igreja.
A igreja fica na praça central.
The church is on the main square.
present → presente: both a gift and the here and now.
Comprei um presente para a minha mãe.
I bought a gift for my mom.
Not a cart! Uma carta is a letter you mail. Also a playing card: jogar cartas.
Recebi uma carta da minha avó.
I got a letter from my grandmother.
lodge → loja: a little booth for selling. Loja de roupas = clothing store.
HOH-pah (r at the start sounds like h)
robe → roupa. Lavar roupa = do laundry.
I need to do the laundry today.
Latin lucta, as in reluctant (struggling against). A luta continua = the struggle goes on.
camera → câmera. Câmera do celular = phone camera.
A câmera do meu celular quebrou.
Used for ANY teacher, even in first grade, not only a university professor.
O professor passou muita lição de casa.
The teacher gave a lot of homework.
demonstrate → mostrar. Me mostra! = Show me!
Vou te mostrar minhas fotos da viagem.
I'll show you my trip photos.
reunion → reunião: people re-united. Tenho reunião = I have a meeting.
proof / prove → prova. Prova de matemática = math test.
Tomorrow I have an English test.
Latin trahere, as in tractor: something that pulls things to you. Traz! = Bring it!
"Oh, LOOK!" says the EYE. Olho por olho = an eye for an eye.
Abre o olho, está vindo um carro!
Watch out, a car is coming!
From chamar: something called. In offices, abrir um chamado = open a support ticket.
Abri um chamado para consertar o computador.
I opened a ticket to fix the computer.
traverse → através. Através de = by means of, through.
Soube da notícia através de uma amiga.
I heard the news through a friend.
Latin lex, as in legal and legislation. Lei Seca = Brazil's zero-tolerance drink-driving law.
A lei é igual para todos.
The law is the same for everyone.
bank / bench → banco: both come from an old money-changer's bench.
Preciso ir ao banco antes das quatro.
I need to go to the bank before four.
Weekdays are numbered from Sunday: segunda-feira = second day = Monday. Short form: segunda.
Na segunda eu começo a dieta.
On Monday I'm starting my diet.
to touch / to play (instrument) / to ring
touch → tocar. Tocar violão = play the guitar; o telefone tocou = the phone rang.
Ele sabe tocar violão muito bem.
He can play the guitar very well.
Latin mensis, as in menstrual and semester. Mês que vem = next month.
paper → papel, final l like w. Also a role: o papel principal = the lead role.
Me empresta uma folha de papel?
Can you lend me a sheet of paper?
Latin somnium, as in insomnia. Also a cream-filled doughnut sold in every padaria.
Meu sonho é conhecer o Japão.
My dream is to visit Japan.
bar → bar. In Brazil, a boteco is a simple neighborhood bar.
Vamos tomar uma cerveja no bar?
Shall we have a beer at the bar?
Latin populus, as in population and popular. O povo brasileiro = the Brazilian people.
O povo foi às ruas comemorar.
The people took to the streets to celebrate.
center → centro. Ir ao centro = go downtown.
O museu fica no centro da cidade.
The museum is in the city center.
converse → conversar. Precisamos conversar = we need to talk.
We need to talk about the trip.
Use protetor para proteger a pele.
Use sunscreen to protect your skin.
From beber: what you drink. Bebida alcoólica = alcoholic drink.
What would you like to drink?
base → base, but the s sounds like z.
A base do bolo é de chocolate.
"Nah, more RAH-da!" Cupid insists: she's his GIRLFRIEND. From namorar, to date.
Ele vai apresentar a namorada para a família.
He's going to introduce his girlfriend to the family.
Ela trabalha numa empresa de tecnologia.
She works at a tech company.
"Meh, TAH-gee": you only get HALF the cake. Pela metade = halfway.
I ate half the pizza by myself.
interesting → interessante: double s, ends in -ante.
"Ka-EAR!" the sound of something FALLING and smacking your ear. Caiu! = It fell!
Cuidado para não cair na escada.
Be careful not to fall on the stairs.
grace → engraçado: full of graceful fun. Que engraçado! = How funny!
Latin digitus, as in digit (fingers were the first calculators). Dedo do pé = toe.
I cut my finger while cooking.
"MEN-cheer": the MEN cheer, but they're LYING. Mentira = a lie.
You don't need to lie to me.
coast / costal → costas: ribs line the back. Always plural: dor nas costas = back pain.
French clé / clavier: keys to open things. Chave do carro = car key.
Esqueci a chave dentro de casa.
I left the key inside the house.
diverting / diversion → divertido. Foi muito divertido! = It was so much fun!
The outing was a lot of fun.
scribe / scribble → escrever. Escreve aqui seu nome.
Can you write your name here?
apartment → apartamento. Brazilians shorten it to apê.
Qual é a sua posição no time?
What's your position on the team?
Latin caelum, as in celestial. Céu azul = blue sky.
cable → cabo. Also a cape: Cabo Frio. Ao cabo de = at the end of.
receive → receber. Recebi sua mensagem = I got your message.
Você vai receber o pacote amanhã.
motive → motivo. Por que motivo? = For what reason?
Qual foi o motivo da briga?
What was the reason for the fight?
Latin optimus, as in optimal and optimist. Ótimo! = Great!
Spanish sombra, as in sombrero: the hat that makes SHADE.
Vamos sentar na sombra da árvore.
Let's sit in the shade of the tree.
street / strata → estrada: the Roman paved road. Pé na estrada = hit the road.
A estrada para a praia estava cheia.
The road to the beach was packed.
"SHAY-o": a SHAY (cart) loaded FULL. Estou cheio = I'm full (after eating).
O ônibus está cheio, vamos esperar o próximo.
The bus is full, let's wait for the next one.
company → companhia. Obrigado pela companhia = thanks for the company.
Masculine of namorada: the BOYfriend. Dia dos Namorados in Brazil is June 12.
O namorado dela mora em outra cidade.
Her boyfriend lives in another city.
north → norte. O Norte = Brazil's Amazon region.
Belém fica no norte do Brasil.
Belém is in the north of Brazil.
explain / explicit → explicar. Pode explicar de novo?
Pode explicar de novo, por favor?
apprentice / apprehend → aprender: an apprentice learns.
I want to learn to dance forró.
"KEN-chee": Ken and Barbie on a HOT beach. Água quente = hot water.
"SIGH-ah": she sighs over her new SKIRT. Also the command Saia! = Get out! (from sair).
Not father in the family sense (that's pai)! Only the Catholic priest, like Spanish padre.
vest / vestment → vestido: clothing. Vestido de noiva = wedding dress.
Ela usou um vestido vermelho na festa.
She wore a red dress to the party.
machine → máquina. Máquina de lavar = washing machine.
appear → parecer. Parece que vai chover = it looks like rain.
Spanish izquierda. À esquerda = on the left. Also the political Left.
Turn left at the traffic light.
avó (open o, like 'awe') is grandma; avô (closed o) is grandpa. Os avós = grandparents.
Minha avó faz um bolo de fubá delicioso.
My grandma makes a delicious cornmeal cake.
confide / confidence → confiar. Confio em você = I trust you.
content → contente: happy with what you have.
I was glad about the news.
Spanish frío. Estou com frio = I'm cold. Frio is also a noun: o frio.
a (to) + onde (where): to where. Aonde você vai? = Where are you going?
Where are you going on vacation?
anniversary → aniversário, but in Brazil it mostly means birthday. Feliz aniversário!
function → funcionar. Não funciona = it doesn't work.
French sud, Spanish sur. Rio Grande do Sul = Big River of the South.
Faz frio no sul do Brasil.
It's cold in the south of Brazil.
carnivore / carnal → carne. Carne de porco = pork.
vendor / vending machine → vender. Vende-se = for sale.
They want to sell the house.
a + baixo (low): downward. Abaixo de zero = below zero.
A temperatura ficou abaixo de zero.
Feminine of direito: à direita = on the right. Also the political Right.
The pharmacy is on the right.
cavalry / cavalier → cavalo. Andar a cavalo = ride a horse.
Meu tio tem um cavalo no sítio.
My uncle has a horse at his farm.
